LESSON: PRODUCT PROCESSING AND VALUE ADDITION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship
Topic 3.2: Product Processing and Value Addition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Product Processing and Value Addition, part of Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: How does value addition enhance nutrition and food security?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. suggest methods of value addition for selected agricultural produce,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Product Processing and Value Addition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. carry out processing of selected crop produce,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Product Processing and Value Addition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. carry out home-based packaging and branding of processed agricultural products,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Product Processing and Value Addition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appraise ethical issues in the processing and value addition processes. Learner is guided in purposive group, pair or individually to: ● use digital and non-digital resources to search for information and suggest methods applicable for value addition of selected agricultural produce. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any alternative functional body part or appropriate assistive technology to search. Learners with postural difficulties could be appropriately positioned to enhance access to the devices. Adjust glare on the digital devices’ screens How does value addition enhance nutrition and food security? 52 appropriately for learners who are sensitive to light , ● discuss with resource person on use of applicable methods/techniques to carry out processing of agricultural produce of plant origin such as vegetables, nuts, fruits, cereals, tubers and pulses into Jam, butter, marmalade, ketchup, juices, flour, puree/concentrate of semi - solid fruit extracts, crisps among others. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech/ write/ type/ or use digital devices with text -to -speech software to share own opinion , ● discuss with resource person applicable 53 methods/techniques to carry out processing of produce of animal origin such as honey, milk, hides and skins, meat or fish. ● visit market outlets to observe and study applicable methods of carrying out home-based packaging and branding of processed agricultural products and then, implement possible initiatives in school. Learners with mobility difficulties could use assistive technology for movement, ● discuss and present ethical concerns in processing and value addition of various agricultural produce. Core Competences to be developed: ● Self-efficacy: learner develops self-confidence and realises own potential when carrying out home-based packaging and branding of processed agricultural products. 54 ● Critical thinking and problem solving: learner develops researching skills when searching for information on applicable methods of value addition of selected agricultural produce. 55

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Product Processing and Value Addition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Responsibility: learner takes care of other learners’ items and products when undertaking a project on value addition of

agricultural produce.

● Peace: learner co-exists harmoniously when undertaking project tasks on selected value addition processes and making

exhibitions of value-added products.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Life skills: learner demonstrates peaceful conflict management skills when carrying out a project on selected value addition

processes.

● Consumer education: learner develops consumer awareness when discussing and presenting ethical concerns in

processing and value addition of agricultural produce to protect consumers or users.

Suggested Learning Resources: Source of heat (care should be taken for learners with health issues such as numbness) cutting

tools with enhanced grip, crop and animal produce to be processed such as milk, honey, hides and vegetable produce such as

fruits, cereals and nuts, Adapted computers with appropriate accessibility features, Appropriate applications/ software,

Ergonomic and head operated mouse and footboards, Writing resources, Positioning devices, ICT tools with appropriate

accessibility features, Other related services (physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, learner support)
